## Deferred

Deferred means the boundary is outside a current universal protocol guarantee; it does not mean the risk is absent.

| ID | Threat component | Scope | Deferral class | Boundary and rationale | Normative source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SEC-009` | **Generic EXT-ALERTS sender authenticity** — A receiver may want proof that a generic ALERT came from an authorized or authenticated alerting principal. | `future_version` | `requires_future_versioned_semantics` | Current EXT-ALERTS explicitly permits any sender to emit ALERT, so a universal sender-authentication rejection rule would strengthen the protocol incompatibly. Residual boundary: Generic EXT-ALERTS has no universal authorized-sender set; deployments or selected authenticated profiles must supply that policy. | [`docs/extensions/RFC_EXT_ALERTS.md`](../docs/extensions/RFC_EXT_ALERTS.md) |
| `SEC-014` | **OBJECT_RESYNC object-existence concealment** — NOT_FOUND may disclose whether an object exists when a deployment would prefer ACCESS_DENIED. | `policy_dependent` | `local_policy` | EXT-OBJECT-RESYNC permits ACCESS_DENIED instead of NOT_FOUND based on policy; making concealment universal would reject currently conformant implementations. Residual boundary: The protocol represents ACCESS_DENIED, but the choice between ACCESS_DENIED and NOT_FOUND remains the responder's selected local policy. | [`docs/extensions/RFC_EXT_OBJECT_RESYNC.md`](../docs/extensions/RFC_EXT_OBJECT_RESYNC.md) |
| `SEC-015` | **OBJECT_RESYNC amplification and resource exhaustion** — Object retrieval can consume bandwidth, storage, CPU, or request capacity at deployment scale. | `deployment_only` | `deployment_control` | The RFC's DoS/amplification mitigation is SHOULD-level guidance and defines no universal rate or byte limit that M67 can enforce compatibly. Residual boundary: Deployments must select authentication, quotas, byte budgets, concurrency limits, and rate controls appropriate to their threat environment. | [`docs/extensions/RFC_EXT_OBJECT_RESYNC.md`](../docs/extensions/RFC_EXT_OBJECT_RESYNC.md)<br>[`security_review/OPS_HARDENING_GUIDE.md`](../security_review/OPS_HARDENING_GUIDE.md) |
| `SEC-018` | **Arbitrary semantic secret classification** — Human-readable ALERT, evidence, or application text may contain domain-specific secrets not identifiable from syntax alone. | `policy_dependent` | `non_machine_decidable_without_policy` | AICP 0.1 defines no universal taxonomy that can decide whether arbitrary application text is a secret; a global regex would create false protocol claims. Residual boundary: A deployment must select a data-classification and redaction policy for its own business data and secret types. | [`docs/extensions/RFC_EXT_ALERTS.md`](../docs/extensions/RFC_EXT_ALERTS.md)<br>[`security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md`](../security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md) |
| `SEC-026` | **Independent organizational identity and remote attestation** — A repository evidence subject may self-declare build identity without proving independent organizational control or remotely attested hardware state. | `future_version` | `requires_future_versioned_semantics` | Current AICP evidence binds declared subjects and exact artifacts but defines neither a remote-attestation protocol nor an organizational-independence authority. Residual boundary: Consumers must establish organizational identity and hardware/runtime trust through external systems when required. | [`security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md`](../security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md)<br>[`docs/interop/AICP_Compatibility_Claims_and_Evidence.md`](../docs/interop/AICP_Compatibility_Claims_and_Evidence.md) |
| `SEC-030` | **Endpoint, key-custody, and host compromise** — A compromised endpoint, stolen signing key, or hostile host/runtime can act with the authority available to that component. | `deployment_only` | `deployment_control` | Protocol signatures and exact bindings cannot guarantee that endpoints, private keys, or their host runtime are uncompromised. Residual boundary: Deployments remain responsible for endpoint hardening, runtime isolation, key custody, rotation, and incident response. | [`security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md`](../security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md)<br>[`docs/security/SECURITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md`](../docs/security/SECURITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md) |
| `SEC-031` | **Production DDoS resistance and universal rate limiting** — Protocol endpoints can be exhausted by transport-scale or application-scale request volume. | `deployment_only` | `deployment_control` | AICP defines no universal traffic budget and does not guarantee internet-scale DDoS resistance. Residual boundary: Operators must select network controls, quotas, authentication, autoscaling, circuit breakers, and rate limits for their environment. | [`security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md`](../security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md)<br>[`security_review/OPS_HARDENING_GUIDE.md`](../security_review/OPS_HARDENING_GUIDE.md) |
| `SEC-032` | **Correctness of arbitrary local policy** — A conformant implementation may select a local authorization, privacy, or enforcement policy that is unsuitable for its deployment. | `policy_dependent` | `local_policy` | Deterministic protocol conformance can validate selected-policy structure and outcomes but cannot decide whether an arbitrary local policy is correct. Residual boundary: Policy owners must validate selected rules, data classifications, authorities, and exception handling against deployment requirements. | [`security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md`](../security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md)<br>[`docs/security/SECURITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md`](../docs/security/SECURITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md) |
| `SEC-033` | **Confidentiality of arbitrary application payloads** — Base AICP payloads may contain application data whose confidentiality depends on the selected profile and transport deployment. | `policy_dependent` | `local_policy` | The base protocol does not promise confidentiality for arbitrary application payloads without an appropriate selected profile and deployment controls. Residual boundary: Deployments must select appropriate confidentiality profiles, transport protection, access controls, retention, and redaction policy. | [`security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md`](../security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md)<br>[`docs/security/SECURITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md`](../docs/security/SECURITY_BEST_PRACTICES.md) |
| `SEC-034` | **Independent external security review** — Internal tests and review artifacts do not substitute for assessment by an independent external reviewer. | `deployment_only` | `independent_external_review` | Independent review requires a real third-party engagement and contract-complete report; M67 and its internal evidence cannot manufacture that external fact. Residual boundary: No completed contracted independent-review artifact exists in the repository. | [`security_review/external_reviews/README.md`](../security_review/external_reviews/README.md)<br>[`SECURITY.md`](../SECURITY.md) |
| `SEC-035` | **Model truthfulness and semantic correctness** — An agent or model can produce false, misleading, or semantically incorrect content in a structurally conformant message. | `policy_dependent` | `non_machine_decidable_without_policy` | AICP validates protocol structure and selected deterministic rules; it cannot universally decide whether arbitrary model output is truthful. Residual boundary: Applications remain responsible for model evaluation, human oversight, source verification, and domain-specific correctness controls. | [`security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md`](../security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md) |
| `SEC-036` | **CAPNEG declaration authority and truthfulness** — A participant may make a syntactically valid capability declaration that is unauthorized or untruthful about the implementation behind it. | `policy_dependent` | `local_policy` | CAPNEG deterministically binds the latest declarations and negotiated result but does not define a universal organizational authority for declaration truthfulness. Residual boundary: Deployments must authenticate principals and decide which declaration authorities and attestations they trust. | [`docs/extensions/RFC_EXT_CAPNEG.md`](../docs/extensions/RFC_EXT_CAPNEG.md)<br>[`docs/extensions/RFC_EXT_CAPNEG_v0.2.md`](../docs/extensions/RFC_EXT_CAPNEG_v0.2.md)<br>[`security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md`](../security_review/SECURITY_ASSUMPTIONS.md) |

## Interpretation boundary

Covered rows establish only the protocol-observable behavior named in the row and exercised by the linked owning evidence. Deferred rows preserve deployment, local-policy, future-version, and independent-review boundaries without turning guidance or optional behavior into compatibility-rejecting rules.
